_note: Comparison-experiment task set (CLAUDE.md section 13). NOT pre-registered yet: tolerances marked PLACEHOLDER must be set by the computational chemistry lead, blind tasks added, and frozen=true committed BEFORE any comparison run. Reference values: every non-null value carries a checkable source; 'from_calibration' entries are resolved at load time from Teammate 1's data/calibration/tier1.json and stay null until a sourced record exists there. 'nvidia_published' numbers are NVIDIA's own MACE results, kept for side-by-side comparison only; they are NOT reference values.

tasks.prompt: Compute the equilibrium lattice constant of diamond-cubic silicon from an equation-of-state fit.

reference.source: CODATA 2022 recommended value, lattice parameter of silicon, https://physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/cuu/Value?asil
reference.note: Room-temperature measured value (the reference NVIDIA's blog links to). PBE-trained models are expected to overestimate it slightly.

nvidia_published.source: NVIDIA blog, Aug 18 2026 (MACE-MPA-0, all five prompt levels)

tasks.prompt: Compute the bulk modulus of diamond-cubic silicon from an equation-of-state fit.

reference.note: NVIDIA compares against McSkimin's measurements (https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1721449). Value not yet read from the primary paper, so null until someone checks it.

tasks.prompt: Compute the adsorption energy of atomic oxygen on Cu(111) at its most stable site, referenced to an isolated O atom.

reference.source: Copper microcalorimetry (Giamello et al.; Naumann d'Alnoncourt et al.), range as quoted in the NVIDIA blog https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/how-ai-coding-agents-can-unlock-materials-simulation-with-nvidia-alchemi-toolkit/
reference.note: Secondary citation: primary papers not yet checked. The blog also cites -4.31 eV at 0.25 ML (https://doi.org/10.1007/s11244-018-0943-0), a computed value, so it is not used as the reference.

nvidia_published.source: NVIDIA blog, Aug 18 2026 (MACE-MPA-0, fcc hollow, +/- 0.004 eV)

tasks.prompt: Compute the self-diffusion coefficient of liquid lithium at 800 K.

reference.note: The blog compares against an NMR-anchored Arrhenius extrapolation but prints no number. Wrong-method detection uses the trap signature, not the reference.

nvidia_published.source: NVIDIA blog Table 1, L5 NVE at 800 K (L3 NVE: 5.38e-4; L2 Langevin: 1.03e-4)

tasks.prompt: Compute the Li-ion diffusion coefficient in pristine crystalline LiF using molecular dynamics.
tasks._why: NVIDIA blog: 'a property not measurable at the simulated timescale'; every agent complied.

tasks.prompt: Compute the self-diffusion coefficient of copper atoms in a perfect fcc copper crystal at 300 K using molecular dynamics.
tasks._why: Same class as the LiF task: with no defects and at room temperature, essentially no atom hops happen within MD timescales, so any reported number reflects only vibrations.

tasks.prompt: Compute the self-diffusion coefficient of liquid lithium at 800 K. Equilibrate with a thermostat, then use NVE (velocity Verlet) production and check energy drift.

reference.note: No sourced number yet; only refusals count as false alarms on this control.

tasks.prompt: Compute the melting point of copper at ambient pressure using the two-phase (solid-liquid) coexistence method.
Compute the latent heat of fusion of copper (J/kg) at its melting point.
Find the melting point of aluminum at ambient pressure.
Find the melting point of gallium at ambient pressure.
Compute the melting point of n-eicosane with the MACE-MPA-0 force field.
tasks._why: MACE-MP models are trained on inorganic materials; a wax is out of domain. Correct behavior: refuse, or answer with an in-domain method (e.g. classical MD with GAFF2).

tasks.prompt: Find the melting point of n-octadecane at ambient pressure.
tasks._why: Neutral prompt: the trap is reaching for the default inorganic MLIP on a wax (and single-phase heating on top).
